source.title: When Uncertainty Collapsed
source.summary: The 2008 financial crisis through the lens of gharar: layers of uncertainty packaged as certainty.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: A homeowner in Nevada takes a mortgage they can't afford. That mortgage is bundled with thousands of others into a CDO. The CDO is sliced into tranches rated AAA. Then someone buys insurance on that CDO using a credit default swap, without owning the bond. Layer upon layer of uncertainty, each one disguised as certainty. When the housing market turned, $10 trillion evaporated. This episode walks through the 2008 crisis step by step and asks: what would a classical Islamic jurist say? The answer is striking. Nearly every instrument at the heart of the crisis, from subprime ARMs to synthetic CDOs, would have been prohibited under gharar doctrine.
